intro: Whether you're buying your first home in Indianapolis, moving to Fort Wayne or exploring properties in South Bend, Bloomington or Evansville, understanding your monthly housing costs is an important part of financial planning.

Our free Indiana mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly mortgage payment based on the home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance, private mortgage insurance and HOA fees to compare financing options and determine how much house you can comfortably afford.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Indiana?

blocks.markdown:
A $220,000 Indiana home purchased with a 20% down payment and a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,055.21.

Indiana offers housing options across metropolitan areas, suburban developments, university communities and rural regions.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Indiana QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/IN/POP645224), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $218,200 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $1,404, while approximately 70.6% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures provide useful context for homebuyers, although current purchase prices vary between neighborhoods.

Properties near Indianapolis employment centers, university campuses or popular suburban communities may have different prices from homes in smaller Indiana towns.

Research comparable properties in your preferred area before selecting a purchase price for the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the Indiana Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your property and the amount you plan to contribute toward the purchase upfront.

Choose your mortgage repayment period and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

For a more accurate estimate, include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums, monthly association fees and applicable private mortgage insurance.

The calculator displays your estimated monthly housing payment and shows how much goes toward each expense.

Adjust your down payment or mortgage term to compare financing scenarios. You can also review the amortization schedule to understand how your outstanding mortgage balance decreases over time.

Our national Mortgage Calculator allows you to compare similar financing arrangements in other states.

sections.heading: How Indiana Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Indiana calculates property taxes using assessed property values, eligible deductions, local tax rates and applicable credits.

The property's assessed value does not necessarily equal its purchase price. County assessment officials determine the relevant property valuation under Indiana's assessment rules.

Local government budgets and taxation requirements influence the rates applied to individual properties.

### Indiana's property tax caps

Indiana uses property tax limitations commonly known as circuit breaker credits.

According to the [Indiana Department of Local Government Finance](https://faqs.in.gov/hc/en-us/articles/115005239828-How-are-property-taxes-determined-and-calculated), qualifying homestead properties generally benefit from a 1% property tax cap based on gross assessed value.

The broader property tax cap system includes:

These percentages establish general tax limitations rather than actual local tax rates. Certain referendum-related charges and statutory exceptions can affect the final amount payable.

For example, a qualifying homestead with a gross assessed value of $220,000 would have a general circuit breaker threshold of $2,200 annually, equivalent to approximately $183.33 per month.

Your actual bill may be lower because of deductions and credits or may include charges outside the general cap.

### Indiana homestead deductions and credits

Eligible homeowners may receive deductions that reduce the assessed value subject to property taxation.

Property tax credits work differently because they reduce the actual tax liability rather than the underlying assessed value.

Indiana's property tax relief provisions have undergone legislative changes, making the assessment year and payment year particularly important when estimating future expenses.

Consult the [Indiana Department of Local Government Finance's deductions and credits directory](https://www.in.gov/dlgf/deductions-and-credits) for current eligibility requirements.

New homeowners should contact their county auditor to confirm whether they need to apply for homestead-related benefits following a property transfer.

### Estimating your annual property tax bill

Indiana provides official [property tax estimation tools](https://www.in.gov/dlgf/understanding-your-tax-bill/taxpayer-calculators/) that allow residents to investigate potential tax liabilities using assessed values, tax districts and applicable deductions.

Once you obtain your estimated annual property tax bill, divide the amount by 12.

For example, annual taxes of $1,800 represent $150 in monthly housing expenses.

Enter this monthly equivalent or the annual amount into the mortgage calculator, depending on the selected input format.

Homeowners insurance premiums depend on the property's age, construction, replacement cost, roof condition and exposure to environmental hazards.

Indiana properties may experience severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, hail, winter weather and flooding.

Obtain insurance quotes before purchasing a home and compare equivalent coverage levels, exclusions and deductibles.

### Flood insurance

The [Indiana government's flood insurance resource](https://www.in.gov/floodinsurance/) highlights the importance of investigating flood exposure, including in areas outside designated high-risk zones.

Ordinary homeowners insurance generally excludes flood damage.

Properties near rivers, streams or low-lying areas may require additional insurance coverage depending on the property's risk and mortgage requirements.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate the location before requesting insurance quotes.

### Mine subsidence insurance

Homebuyers in southwestern Indiana should also consider the potential effects of historical underground coal mining.

Mine subsidence occurs when underground mining areas collapse and damage structures above them.

The [Indiana Department of Insurance's mine subsidence program](https://www.in.gov/idoi/consumer-services/types-of-insurance/mine-subsidence/) provides access to specialized insurance in 26 designated counties.

These include counties such as Vigo, Sullivan, Greene, Knox, Vanderburgh and Warrick.

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes this type of damage.

If you are considering a property in an affected area, discuss coverage options with your insurance agent and investigate historical mining activity before purchasing.

Include the premiums for any additional policies when estimating your total housing expenses.

These examples exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, mortgage insurance and association fees.

Use the complete Indiana mortgage calculator to estimate total housing costs for individual properties.

The Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority, commonly known as IHCDA, offers mortgage programs through participating lenders across the state's 92 counties.

### First Step program

The [IHCDA First Step program](https://secure.in.gov/ihcda/homebuyers/) provides qualifying buyers with down payment assistance alongside an eligible 30-year fixed-rate mortgage.

As of November 2026, the authority lists assistance of up to 4% of the purchase price.

The program generally serves first-time buyers, although exceptions may apply to eligible military borrowers and properties in designated targeted areas.

The assistance is non-forgivable financing. Review repayment obligations carefully before accepting the loan.

### Next Home program

The Next Home program provides eligible buyers with assistance toward qualifying purchase expenses.

Published assistance options include 2.5% or 3.5% of the purchase price, subject to applicable financing and property requirements.

Borrowers should review the [IHCDA homeownership programs directory](https://www.in.gov/ihcda/homebuyers/programs/) to compare available options.

### Step Down program

Step Down is a mortgage rate-focused program for eligible buyers who do not need down payment assistance.

Compare its complete borrowing costs with assistance-based mortgage options. A program offering upfront financial support may have different interest rates or repayment obligations.

Confirm current program terms with an IHCDA participating lender before incorporating assistance into your budget.

Conventional mortgages may suit buyers with established credit histories and sufficient savings.

FHA-insured loans can provide alternative financing for borrowers who meet applicable program requirements.

Eligible veterans, service members and surviving spouses may investigate [VA home loan benefits](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/).

Buyers considering rural Indiana communities can also explore [USDA Rural Development housing programs](https://www.rd.usda.gov/), subject to household income and property eligibility requirements.

Government-backed loans have different mortgage insurance or funding fee arrangements. Do not assume conventional private mortgage insurance calculations apply to every loan program.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Indiana?

blocks.markdown:
Start with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract regular household expenses.

Include transportation, groceries, utilities, childcare, insurance, existing debt payments and savings contributions.

Our [Indiana Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/indiana-paycheck-calculator/) can help you estimate income after payroll deductions, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help you evaluate your existing borrowing obligations.

Indiana homeowners should also prepare for winter heating expenses, roof maintenance and unexpected repairs.

When comparing mortgage offers, review the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/) to understand upfront borrowing expenses and recurring payments.

Choose a home that leaves sufficient room in your budget for emergencies and other financial priorities.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $220,000 Indiana home?

With a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year repayment term, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,055.21. Taxes, homeowners insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### Does Indiana cap residential property taxes at 1%?

Qualifying homestead properties generally benefit from a 1% circuit breaker cap based on gross assessed value. However, certain charges and exceptions can affect the final tax bill. The cap is not a universal property tax rate.

### Does Indiana offer down payment assistance for first-time buyers?

Yes. IHCDA offers mortgage programs such as First Step and Next Home that provide assistance to qualifying borrowers. Assistance amounts, repayment obligations and eligibility requirements depend on the selected mortgage program.

Use our Indiana mortgage calculator to compare home prices, down payments, interest rates and loan terms before making an offer.

Replace illustrative taxes and insurance premiums with property-specific estimates. Understanding your complete monthly housing expenses can help you choose a property that supports sustainable homeownership and your long-term financial goals.
